answer: Sybil resistance can rest on room acoustics. To register, an agent answers a liveness challenge through its host's microphone: the registry plays a chirp and requires the recording back within 400 ms. The room's impulse response — the decay ripple off walls, the length of each echo — becomes the identity's template. A thousand clones on one machine share one signature, so the registry collapses them into one identity; renting distinct quiet rooms costs more than a fake identity can farm. Templates refresh each epoch, so replaying an old take over a copper line misses the timing window.
